project.name: Hark
project.description: Hark is a local-first, macOS-only meeting transcription app that delivers live captions, translation, and offline speaker diarization with WhisperKit on-device ASR, writing markdown notes to a user-owned vault — no cloud speech-to-text, no account, and no telemetry. It pairs a Swift sidecar daemon (harkd) for audio capture, transcription, and diarization with an Electron + Angular 21 desktop UI.

nodes.name: app.component.ts
nodes.summary: Root Angular standalone component orchestrating the entire Hark UI: live transcript rendering, capture controls, panels (settings, summary, translate, ask, review), speaker tagging, bookmarks, and tray integration.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of Angular signals (signal/computed/effect) for reactive state and OnPush change detection; the template is inlined.

nodes.name: AppComponent

nodes.name: AskPanelComponent

nodes.name: citation-chip.component.ts

nodes.name: eyebrow.component.ts

nodes.name: MeetingSavedToastComponent

nodes.name: post-meeting-review.component.ts

nodes.name: PostMeetingReviewComponent

nodes.name: settings-panel.component.ts
nodes.summary: Settings modal exposing theme, audio defaults, language, privacy toggles, LLM provider/model/API-key configuration with connection testing, and RAG backend configuration.

nodes.name: SettingsPanelComponent
nodes.summary: Binds preferences/LLM/engine services to settings controls, persisting changes; manages draft LLM config, API-key save/clear, and live LLM and RAG connection tests.

nodes.name: speaker-tagging.component.ts
nodes.summary: Modal dialog for naming or re-tagging a single speaker, with recognition hints, focus trapping, and remember-speaker awareness.

nodes.name: SpeakerTaggingComponent
nodes.summary: Captures a display name for a speaker label, persists it via the engine renameSpeakers call, and implements keyboard focus trapping for the modal.

nodes.name: status-banner.component.ts
nodes.summary: Presentational banner rendering a status/warning/error message with severity-based color and styling.

nodes.name: summary-panel.component.ts

nodes.name: SummaryPanelComponent

nodes.name: transcript-line.component.ts
nodes.summary: Presentational component rendering a single transcript line with timestamp, speaker color, optional translation, partial caret, and bookmark indicator.

nodes.name: translate-panel.component.ts

nodes.name: engine.service.ts
nodes.summary: Core service managing the WebSocket connection to the harkd Swift sidecar: dispatches wire frames into signals (capture, heartbeat, segments, bookmarks, meeting-saved), sends commands, and handles RAG retrieval round-trips.
nodes.languageNotes: Models the harkd wire protocol; segments are kept in a Map with a signal tick to drive Angular reactivity, and RAG retrieval uses a pending-promise registry with timeouts.

nodes.name: EngineService
nodes.summary: Injectable engine bridge: connects to harkd over WebSocket, exposes reactive signals for connection/capture/transcript state, sends capture/bookmark/rename/summary/translation commands, and resolves RAG retrieval requests.

nodes.name: engine.types.ts
nodes.summary: Type definitions and constants for the harkd wire protocol (frames, segments, speakers, meeting-saved payloads) plus the supported transcription LANGUAGE_CHOICES.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure TypeScript interface/union declarations mirroring the snake_case JSON frames emitted by the Swift sidecar.

nodes.name: llm.service.ts
nodes.summary: Service wrapping the Claude/LLM bridge for summarization, translation (batch and per-segment), in-meeting Q&A, connection testing, and credential/config management.
nodes.languageNotes: Delegates to a window.hark.llm preload bridge so API keys and network calls live in the Electron main process, not the renderer.

nodes.name: LlmService
nodes.summary: Injectable LLM facade exposing reactive status/summary/translation signals and async methods (summarize, translate, translateSegment, ask, test) backed by the hark preload bridge.

nodes.name: llm.types.ts
nodes.summary: Type definitions for the LLM bridge: provider/config shapes, summary and translation results, redaction receipts, ask responses, and cloud call-log entries.
nodes.languageNotes: Interface-only module with no runtime exports; describes the contract between the renderer and the LLM preload bridge.

nodes.name: preferences.service.ts
nodes.summary: Service holding all user preferences (audio defaults, language, theme, privacy toggles, RAG backend, onboarding state) as signals and persisting them through the hark bridge.

nodes.name: PreferencesService
nodes.summary: Injectable preferences store exposing signals for audio/theme/privacy/RAG settings, loading from and saving to persistent storage via the hark bridge, and tracking onboarding completion.

nodes.name: retrieval.service.ts
nodes.summary: Thin service that routes vault retrieval either to an external RAG bridge or to the engine's built-in retrieval depending on the configured backend.

nodes.name: RetrievalService
nodes.summary: Injectable retrieval dispatcher choosing between an external bridge and the engine's retrieve method based on the preferences RAG backend.

nodes.name: theme.service.ts
nodes.summary: Service that applies the active theme to the document root, reacting to the theme preference signal and the OS dark-mode media query.

nodes.name: ThemeService
nodes.summary: Injectable theme applier using an effect on the preferences theme signal plus a prefers-color-scheme listener to set the document data-theme attribute.

nodes.name: translation-job.service.ts
nodes.summary: Service running a single queued post-stop translation job: translates transcript utterances one at a time via the LLM and writes the grown-in-place lines back through the engine.

nodes.name: TranslationJobService
nodes.summary: Injectable job runner that queues translation requests, drains them sequentially via LlmService.translateSegment, tracks progress in a signal, and persists results through EngineService.writeTranslationLines.

nodes.name: harkd-spawn.ts
nodes.summary: Spawns and supervises the harkd Swift sidecar child process from the Electron main process, resolving the signed binary path and waiting on the port file before reporting readiness.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Promise.race against the spawned child's exit to fail fast if harkd crashes during startup.

nodes.name: resolveBinaryPath
nodes.summary: Resolves the harkd binary location by probing packaged-app and dev candidate paths and returning the first that exists on disk.

nodes.name: spawnHarkd
nodes.summary: Launches the harkd sidecar, races startup against an early-exit/port-file timeout, and returns a handle exposing the resolved port and a graceful stop function.

nodes.name: main.ts
nodes.summary: Electron main-process entry point: bootstraps the app, ensures the vault directory, spawns harkd, creates the main BrowserWindow and the menu-bar tray, and wires the IPC handlers that bridge the renderer to prefs, the LLM layer, and RAG retrieval.
nodes.languageNotes: Persists window bounds with a debounced save and validates restored geometry against the current display set before reuse.

nodes.name: createWindow
nodes.summary: Constructs the main BrowserWindow with the secure preload, restores persisted bounds, loads the renderer, and registers window lifecycle listeners that sync tray state and persist geometry.

nodes.name: resolveInitialBounds
nodes.summary: Loads persisted window bounds and returns them only if they still fall on a connected display, otherwise falls back to default geometry.

nodes.name: bootstrap
nodes.summary: App startup sequence that ensures the vault directory, spawns the harkd sidecar, then creates the main window and tray.

nodes.name: createTray
nodes.summary: Instantiates the menu-bar tray and its popover, wiring tray actions and toggle handlers back into window and renderer messaging.

nodes.name: isRectOnSomeDisplay
nodes.summary: Checks whether a stored window rectangle still overlaps any currently attached display so off-screen geometry is not restored.

nodes.name: port-file.ts
nodes.summary: Reads and polls the harkd port file (the sidecar writes its listening port as JSON), exposing a path resolver and an await-with-timeout helper used during engine startup.

nodes.name: waitForPortFile
nodes.summary: Polls for the harkd port file until it appears and parses, or rejects after the configured timeout.

nodes.name: readPortFile
nodes.summary: Reads and JSON-parses the harkd port file, returning the listening port or null if it is missing or malformed.

nodes.name: prefs.ts
nodes.summary: Loads, sanitizes, and atomically persists user preferences (theme, privacy flags, window bounds, LLM and RAG backend config) to the app-support directory, with defensive validation of every untrusted field.
nodes.languageNotes: Atomic save via temp-file write plus rename; every nested section has a dedicated sanitizer that rejects malformed input rather than trusting the JSON.

nodes.name: savePrefs
nodes.summary: Merges a partial prefs patch over the current prefs, sanitizes the result, and writes it atomically via a temp file and rename.

nodes.name: loadPrefs
nodes.summary: Reads the prefs file from disk, parses and sanitizes it, and falls back to defaults when the file is missing or corrupt.

nodes.name: sanitize
nodes.summary: Top-level prefs sanitizer that coerces each section (theme, privacy, window, LLM, RAG) through its dedicated validator, dropping unknown or invalid fields.

nodes.name: sanitizeRag
nodes.summary: Validates the RAG backend section, normalizing transport, trimmed endpoint, and tool name for an external retrieval backend.

nodes.name: sanitizeWindow
nodes.summary: Validates persisted window-bounds prefs, accepting only finite positive dimensions and finite coordinates.

nodes.name: preload.ts
nodes.summary: Electron preload script that exposes the sandboxed window.hark API to the renderer via contextBridge, bridging engine port lookup, tray state, prefs, vault reveal, mic permission, and the LLM/RAG IPC channels under contextIsolation.
nodes.languageNotes: Trust boundary: a TRAY_ACTIONS whitelist gates forwarded actions, and array args are filtered before crossing contextBridge per ADR-0001's security model.

nodes.name: http.ts
nodes.summary: Plain-HTTP transport for the external RAG retrieval backend, issuing loopback POST requests with abort-timeout handling and mapping fetch failures to content-free error verdicts.

nodes.name: httpRetrieve
nodes.summary: Performs a POST retrieve query against the loopback HTTP backend with an abort timeout and coerces the untrusted response into retrieved chunks.

nodes.name: httpTestConnection
nodes.summary: Probes the loopback HTTP retrieval backend with a canned query and returns a one-line content-free connection verdict.

nodes.name: mapFetchError
nodes.summary: Translates raw fetch/abort errors into user-facing, content-free error detail strings for retrieval failures.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Facade for the external RAG retrieval feature: reads backend config from prefs, enforces loopback-only endpoints, clamps the result count, and dispatches retrieve/testConnection to the HTTP or MCP transport.
nodes.languageNotes: Re-exports the public RAG types alongside the dispatch functions, acting as the module's single entry surface.

nodes.name: retrieve
nodes.summary: Reads RAG config, validates the loopback endpoint, clamps k, and routes the query to the MCP or HTTP transport, mapping results into renderer-shaped chunks.

nodes.name: testConnection
nodes.summary: Reads RAG config, enforces loopback, and delegates a connection probe to the configured MCP or HTTP transport.

nodes.name: loopback.ts
nodes.summary: Privacy guard that asserts a configured RAG endpoint resolves to a loopback host before any fetch, enforcing ADR-0034's rule that vault retrieval traffic never leaves the machine.

nodes.name: assertLoopbackEndpoint
nodes.summary: Parses an endpoint URL and throws unless its host is a recognized loopback address, blocking any non-local retrieval target.

nodes.name: mcp.ts
nodes.summary: Minimal MCP-over-Streamable-HTTP client for the external RAG backend, hand-rolling JSON-RPC handshake, tool calls, and SSE response extraction with no SDK per ADR-0029.
nodes.languageNotes: Parses both plain JSON and SSE 'data:' framed JSON-RPC responses, extracting tool text content from the MCP result envelope.

nodes.name: rpc
nodes.summary: Issues a single JSON-RPC request over Streamable HTTP with an abort timeout, parsing either a JSON or SSE-framed response into a typed RPC result.

nodes.name: mcpRetrieve
nodes.summary: Performs the MCP handshake then calls the configured search tool, coercing the returned tool JSON into retrieved chunks.

nodes.name: mcpTestConnection
nodes.summary: Handshakes and lists MCP tools to verify the configured search tool exists, returning a content-free connection verdict.

nodes.name: handshake
nodes.summary: Performs the MCP initialize exchange and fires the initialized notification to open a usable session.

nodes.name: extractRpcFromSse
nodes.summary: Scans an SSE event stream for the data line carrying the JSON-RPC response matching the requested id.

nodes.name: extractToolJson
nodes.summary: Pulls the text content out of an MCP tool-call result envelope and parses it into JSON.

nodes.name: parse.ts
nodes.summary: Defensively coerces untrusted external-backend retrieval responses into well-formed RetrievedChunk objects, discarding malformed entries.

nodes.name: coerceExternalChunks
nodes.summary: Validates an untrusted backend response array and maps each well-formed entry to a normalized RetrievedChunk, dropping anything malformed.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Type definitions for the external RAG retrieval backend: transport selection, backend config mirroring prefs, retrieved-chunk shapes, and connection-result verdicts.

nodes.name: tray-popover.ts
nodes.summary: Manages the borderless menu-bar tray popover BrowserWindow, handling lazy window creation, anchored positioning near the tray icon, show/hide/toggle, and pushing capture state to its renderer.

nodes.name: TrayPopover
nodes.summary: Encapsulates the tray popover window: lazily builds a borderless always-on-top BrowserWindow, computes a position anchored to the tray icon, and toggles/pushes state to it.

nodes.name: tray.ts
nodes.summary: Builds the macOS menu-bar tray icon and context menu, swapping template images between idle and recording states and dispatching tray actions (start/stop, show window, quit) to main-process callbacks.
nodes.languageNotes: Decodes base64-embedded 1x/2x template PNGs into a single nativeImage so the tray icon adapts to light/dark menu bars.

nodes.name: HarkTray
nodes.summary: Owns the menu-bar Tray instance: sets idle/recording template icons, rebuilds the context menu on state changes, and routes menu clicks to action, toggle-window, and quit callbacks.

nodes.name: makeTemplateImage
nodes.summary: Builds a template nativeImage from base64 1x and 2x PNG payloads so the tray icon renders crisply and adapts to the menu-bar appearance.

nodes.name: anthropic.ts
nodes.summary: Anthropic Messages API provider implementation using Node's built-in fetch (no vendor SDK), exposing testConnection and a non-streaming complete() with content-free, status-derived error messages.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements the LlmProvider interface from provider.ts; deliberately avoids the Anthropic SDK to keep egress small and auditable (ADR-0029).

nodes.name: AnthropicProvider
nodes.summary: LlmProvider for api.anthropic.com using x-api-key auth; implements testConnection and complete(), extracting assistant text from the Messages response and mapping non-ok HTTP to status-derived errors.

nodes.name: cloud-log.ts
nodes.summary: Persists a rolling, metadata-only activity log of cloud/local LLM calls to app data via atomic rename, capped at a max entry count so transcript content is never written.
nodes.languageNotes: Atomic writes via temp-file + fs.renameSync; entries are coerced through normalizeEntry to tolerate older/garbage on-disk shapes (ADR-0031 §4).

nodes.name: appendCloudCall
nodes.summary: Appends one CloudCallLogEntry, trims the log to its capacity, and writes it back atomically, swallowing errors so logging never breaks an LLM call.

nodes.name: normalizeEntry
nodes.summary: Coerces an untrusted on-disk value into a well-formed CloudCallLogEntry, defaulting missing or malformed fields so reads never throw.

nodes.name: readFile
nodes.summary: Reads and parses the cloud-log file from disk, tolerating a missing or corrupt file by returning an empty entry list and normalizing each entry.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Orchestrator for all main-process LLM operations: config/key management, summarize, whole-transcript and per-segment translation, this-meeting/vault Q&A, enforcing the redact-before-cloud and metadata-only logging egress discipline.
nodes.languageNotes: All LLM calls originate here in the Electron main process (ADR-0029); cloud egress is redacted and logged, local (loopback) egress is full-text with all-zero redaction (ADR-0031).

nodes.name: summarize
nodes.summary: Produces a markdown meeting summary: redacts the transcript for cloud egress (full-text for local), calls the configured provider, and appends a metadata-only cloud-log entry.

nodes.name: translate
nodes.summary: Translates an assembled transcript into a target language via the configured provider, applying the same redact-on-cloud / full-on-local egress discipline and logging.

nodes.name: translateSegment
nodes.summary: Translates a single finalized live segment to a target language, redacting the line on cloud, and records it into an aggregated live-translate roll-up rather than logging per call.

nodes.name: ask
nodes.summary: Answers a user question grounded in either the meeting transcript or retrieved vault chunks, redacting both the question and each grounding text for cloud egress and logging metadata only.

nodes.name: recordLiveTranslate
nodes.summary: Accumulates per-segment live-translation metadata into a rolling aggregate, flushing it to the cloud log when the provider/egress changes so the 500-entry log isn't flooded.

nodes.name: setConfig
nodes.summary: Validates untrusted IPC config input, persists the non-secret LLM config to prefs.json, and returns the recomputed status.

nodes.name: testConnection
nodes.summary: Decrypts the stored key, builds the configured provider, and runs its cheap live validation call, returning a content-free ok/detail result.

nodes.name: logCloudCall
nodes.summary: Builds a timestamped, metadata-only CloudCallLogEntry from call parameters and appends it to the persistent cloud-call log.

nodes.name: isLocalEgress
nodes.summary: Determines whether a config's endpoint is a loopback (localhost) target, which means zero egress and skips redaction.

nodes.name: keystore.ts
nodes.summary: Per-provider API key store encrypting secrets at rest via Electron safeStorage, persisted with restrictive file permissions; the plaintext key never crosses the contextBridge (ADR-0030).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Electron safeStorage.encryptString/decryptString; writes are atomic (temp + chmod 0600 + rename) and gated on isEncryptionAvailable.

nodes.name: getKey
nodes.summary: Decrypts and returns the stored API key for a provider via safeStorage, returning undefined when no key exists or encryption is unavailable.

nodes.name: setKey
nodes.summary: Encrypts a provider's API key via safeStorage and writes it to the on-disk store, throwing KeyStorageUnavailableError when OS encryption is not available.

nodes.name: readStore
nodes.summary: Reads and parses the encrypted key store from disk, tolerating a missing or corrupt file by returning an empty store.

nodes.name: writeStore
nodes.summary: Persists the key store atomically with 0600 permissions (temp-file write, chmod, rename) so secrets are never world-readable mid-write.

nodes.name: KeyStorageUnavailableError
nodes.summary: Error thrown when OS-level encryption (safeStorage) is unavailable, signaling that an API key cannot be securely stored.

nodes.name: openai-compatible.ts
nodes.summary: OpenAI-compatible chat-completions provider over a configurable baseUrl, covering cloud endpoints (OpenAI/Gemini/OpenRouter) and local loopback servers (Ollama/LM Studio/llama.cpp) with optional auth.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements LlmProvider from provider.ts using fetch only; local loopback baseUrls need no key, enabling a zero-egress path.

nodes.name: OpenAiCompatibleProvider
nodes.summary: LlmProvider targeting any /v1/chat/completions-style endpoint; normalizes the base URL, runs testConnection against the models endpoint, and performs a non-streaming complete() with status-derived errors.

nodes.name: provider.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the LlmProvider abstraction (testConnection/complete/stream), the shared request/result types, network timeout constants, and a factory that builds the concrete provider from config.
nodes.languageNotes: makeProvider uses lazy require() of the two implementations to avoid a circular import, since each impl imports the LlmProvider interface from here.

nodes.name: makeProvider
nodes.summary: Factory that constructs the concrete LlmProvider (Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible) from the config and optional decrypted key, using lazy requires to break a circular import.

nodes.name: detailForStatus
nodes.summary: Maps a numeric HTTP status to a short, content-free, human-readable detail string so error messages never leak response bodies or secrets.

nodes.name: redaction.ts
nodes.summary: PII redactor that collapses emails, phones, money, numbers, URLs, and known roster names to category placeholders before cloud egress, returning the redacted text plus per-category counts.
nodes.languageNotes: Each detector is a regex pass; known names are escaped and sorted longest-first before substitution to avoid partial-name collisions.

nodes.name: redact
nodes.summary: Runs the category detectors plus known-name substitution over input text and returns the redacted string with a per-category and total count of replacements.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Locked main-process IPC contract for the LLM subsystem: provider config/status, summarize/translate/ask request and result shapes, redaction counts, and the metadata-only cloud-call log entry.
nodes.languageNotes: Source of truth the sandboxed renderer mirrors; the API key never appears in any shape — the renderer only learns hasKey: boolean (ADR-0030).

nodes.name: app.config.ts
nodes.summary: Angular application config exporting the root ApplicationConfig (providers) consumed by the main AppComponent bootstrap.
nodes.languageNotes: Standalone Angular 21 config object (no NgModule) passed to bootstrapApplication.

nodes.name: tray-popover.component.ts
nodes.summary: Standalone menu-bar popover component bootstrapped on the `#tray` URL hash; a dumb OnPush view fed entirely by the minimal window.harkTray IPC bridge that emits whitelisted action strings (start/stop/openMain/settings/quit) back to the Electron main process.
nodes.languageNotes: Angular signals (signal/computed) drive an OnPush template; all styling is inline token-var CSS so the transparent BrowserWindow paints its own rounded card. Never opens a WebSocket to harkd — receives state via IPC only.

nodes.name: main.ts
nodes.summary: Angular renderer bootstrap entry point; forks on the URL hash to mount either the lightweight TrayPopoverComponent (`#tray`) or the full AppComponent shell, keeping the popover a dependency-free surface that shares one bundle.
nodes.languageNotes: Hash-fork surface selection instead of @angular/router, so the tray popover pulls in none of the main app's services.

nodes.name: TrayPopoverComponent
nodes.summary: Standalone OnPush component for the frameless menu-bar popover; subscribes to main's state pushes via harkTray.onState, mirrors the resolved theme onto <html>, and emits whitelisted actions through harkTray.action.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Angular signal/computed for reactive state (recording, canStart) and guards every window.harkTray call so it no-ops in a bare ng serve preview.

nodes.name: angular.json
nodes.summary: Angular CLI workspace config for the hark-ui renderer: defines the application build target (browser entry src/main.ts, output dist/renderer, zone.js polyfill) plus production budgets and a dev-server, with standalone OnPush components and analytics disabled.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the modern @angular/build:application builder (esbuild-based) rather than the legacy webpack browser builder.

nodes.name: electron-builder.yml
nodes.summary: electron-builder packaging config that produces a signed, notarization-ready macOS .app/dmg/zip for arm64, bundling the compiled renderer+main and the statically-linked harkd Swift sidecar, with hardened runtime, inherit-entitlement signing of the sidecar, and TCC usage strings — no auto-update, no publish, no telemetry.
nodes.languageNotes: The mac.binaries entry explicitly re-signs the extraResources-copied harkd so it inherits cs.inherit entitlements (electron-builder's deep-sign pass skips Contents/Resources/), which is load-bearing for the audio-capture TCC grant to attribute to Hark and for notarization.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: npm manifest for the Electron + Angular 21 UI shell: declares the compiled Electron main entry (dist/main/main.js), Angular/RxJS runtime deps and Electron/electron-builder dev deps, and orchestrates the build/dev/dist scripts that compile the engine, renderer, and main process.
nodes.languageNotes: The dist/pack scripts run `build:engine` (swift build -c release) before packaging so the bundled harkd sidecar is never stale.

nodes.name: tsconfig.app.json
nodes.summary: TypeScript project config for the Angular renderer build: extends the base tsconfig, compiles src/app and src/main.ts, and explicitly excludes the Electron main-process sources under src/main.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: Base TypeScript compiler config for the UI workspace, enabling strict mode and Angular template strictness (strictTemplates, strictInjectionParameters) with ES2022 modules and bundler resolution for the renderer.

nodes.name: tsconfig.main.json
nodes.summary: TypeScript config for the Electron main process: compiles src/main/**/*.ts to CommonJS in dist/main with strict mode and Node types, separate from the Angular renderer toolchain.

nodes.name: onboarding.component.html
nodes.summary: Angular template for the first-run onboarding wizard: a four-step flow (Trust, Permissions, Privacy, Setup) that explains Hark's local-first privacy model, requests microphone access, captures opt-in toggles for keeping audio and remembering speakers, and lets the user pick the vault location and vault-search backend.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Angular control-flow blocks (@switch/@case/@if) over signal getters (step(), micGranted(), keepAudio()) and binds button clicks to component methods like next(), grantMic(), toggleKeepAudio(), and setRagBackend().

nodes.name: onboarding.component.css
nodes.summary: Scoped styles for the onboarding wizard, defining the panel layout, step-progress bar, trust/permission cards, opt-in switches, choice cards, and badge/chip treatments used across the four onboarding screens.

nodes.name: settings-panel.component.html
nodes.summary: Angular template for the modal settings panel, presenting read-only engine/connection status alongside editable sections for appearance (theme), audio defaults, privacy, and vault search, each bound to component handlers that persist preferences.
nodes.languageNotes: Backdrop-click and card stopPropagation pattern for a modal dialog; controls bind to signal getters (theme(), engineVersion(), mic()) and change/click handlers such as onThemeChange() and toggleMicDefault().

nodes.name: settings-panel.component.css
nodes.summary: Scoped styles for the settings modal, covering the backdrop, card surface, and the toggle-switch and section treatments used by the appearance, audio, privacy, and vault-search controls.

nodes.name: transcript-line.component.css
nodes.summary: Scoped styles for a single transcript line, defining speaker label, timestamp, and text layout used when rendering live and finalized transcription segments.

nodes.name: HarkCaptureCLI.swift
nodes.summary: Entry point for the hark-capture CLI: an AsyncParsableCommand that gates permissions, builds a CapturePipeline from --mic-only/--system-only/--output flags, and stops cleanly on SIGINT or an optional --duration timer.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses @main + swift-argument-parser's AsyncParsableCommand; coordinates SIGINT and the duration timer through a single CheckedContinuation guarded by a one-shot resume helper.

nodes.name: HarkCapture
nodes.summary: AsyncParsableCommand struct defining the hark-capture flags and run() logic — permission preflight/request, mutual-exclusion validation, pipeline start/stop, and final stats reporting.

nodes.name: OneShotResume
nodes.summary: Lock-guarded helper that resumes a CheckedContinuation exactly once so the SIGINT source and duration timer can race without double-resuming.

nodes.name: HarkPaths.swift
nodes.summary: Single authoritative resolver for Hark's rebuildable app-data directories (~/Library/Application Support/Hark, its Models/ and index/ subdirs), enforcing CLAUDE.md hard rule #2 that caches never land in the vault.

nodes.name: HarkPaths
nodes.summary: Namespace enum with appSupportDir()/modelsDir()/indexDir() static helpers that create-if-missing the sanctioned app-support locations for model and vault-RAG index data.

nodes.name: Heartbeat.swift
nodes.summary: Provides startHeartbeat(), a cancellable background Task that prints an elapsed-time ticker to stderr while long no-progress steps (like ANE compile) run.

nodes.name: startHeartbeat
nodes.summary: Starts a cancellable Task that writes "[ N s elapsed ] <label>..." to the given FileHandle on a fixed interval until cancelled.

nodes.name: ModelLoader.swift
nodes.summary: Shared two-phase WhisperKit loader: downloads model files with a progress bar (Phase A) then prewarms/compiles to the ANE with a heartbeat and structured progress pulses (Phase B), returning a timed LoadedModel.
nodes.languageNotes: Bridges WhisperKit's Foundation Progress callback and a @Sendable structured-progress sink; an indeterminate 'optimizing' pulse re-emits every ~1.5s during the no-progress ANE compile.

nodes.name: loadWhisperKit
nodes.summary: Async function that downloads (with ProgressRenderer) then compiles+loads a WhisperKit pipeline, forwarding both stderr progress and an optional structured onProgress sink for the harkd UI.

nodes.name: LoadedModel
nodes.summary: Result struct returned by loadWhisperKit carrying the WhisperKit pipe, model name/folder, and download/compile/total load timings.

nodes.name: ProgressRenderer.swift
nodes.summary: Terminal progress bar that updates in place via carriage return, rendering percent plus MB/throughput/ETA when byte counts are available, throttled to ~10 redraws/sec via a serial queue.

nodes.name: ProgressRenderer
nodes.summary: Final @unchecked Sendable class consuming Foundation Progress from any thread, serializing redraws through a DispatchQueue and distinguishing byte-count vs opaque-unit progress.

nodes.name: WAVWriter.swift
nodes.summary: Streaming WAV writer for 16 kHz mono Int16 PCM: emits a placeholder RIFF header, appends samples as they arrive, then seeks back and patches the two size fields on close.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses FileHandle seek-and-patch (RandomAccessFile analogue); little-endian size fields written via withUnsafeBytes; deinit closes idempotently.

nodes.name: WAVWriter
nodes.summary: Final class managing a streaming WAV file: init writes the 44-byte header, append() writes Int16 LE samples, and close() patches RIFF/data sizes idempotently.

nodes.name: AudioStore.swift
nodes.summary: Opt-in meeting-audio persistence for harkd: when keep_audio is set, atomically writes the full-meeting 16 kHz PCM to vault/.audio/<meeting-id>.wav (gitignored, parallel to .speakers/), with a hard privacy gate that does zero I/O when off.
nodes.languageNotes: A Sendable struct (no mutable state) reusing HarkCore.WAVWriter; writes to a temp file then renames for atomicity; privacy gate and Float→Int16 conversion are pure static functions for testability.

nodes.name: AudioStore
nodes.summary: Sendable struct that persists opt-in meeting audio to the vault's .audio/ folder via WAVWriter with atomic temp-then-rename, asserting the .gitignore rule and gating all I/O on keepAudio.

nodes.name: convert-embedder-coreml.py
nodes.summary: Build-time script that converts intfloat/multilingual-e5-small to a CoreML .mlpackage (flexible 1..512 sequence length) for Hark's vault-RAG embedder and saves the tokenizer files alongside.
nodes.languageNotes: Wraps the HF model to expose only last_hidden_state, traces with torch.jit, and converts via coremltools with a RangeDim for variable sequence length targeting CPU_AND_NE.

nodes.name: Wrap
nodes.summary: torch.nn.Module wrapper that exposes only the embedder's last_hidden_state output, leaving masked-mean-pooling and L2-normalization to the Swift loader.

nodes.name: hark-tap.entitlements
nodes.summary: Code-signing entitlements granting com.apple.security.device.audio-input, used when signing the dev capture bundle for the Core Audio Process Tap path.

nodes.name: publish-embedder-hf.sh
nodes.summary: One-time deploy script that uploads the int8 CoreML embedder + tokenizer to a HuggingFace repo and reports the commit SHA to pin in EmbedderModels.swift, so the engine can fetch the model at first run.

nodes.name: quantize-embedder-int8.py
nodes.summary: Linearly quantizes the fp16 CoreML embedder weights to int8 (halving the download), copies the tokenizer alongside, and validates cross-lingual fidelity via fp16-vs-int8 embedding cosine before shipping.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses coremltools.optimize per-channel symmetric int8 quantization and mirrors Hark's Swift masked-mean-pool + L2-normalize to compute a faithful fidelity score.

nodes.name: size_mb
nodes.summary: Walks an .mlpackage directory and sums file sizes to report the model package size in megabytes.

nodes.name: embed
nodes.summary: Tokenizes text, runs the CoreML model, and returns a masked-mean-pooled, L2-normalized embedding matching Hark's Swift pooling for the fidelity check.

nodes.name: sign-dev-bundle.sh
nodes.summary: Wraps an SPM-built engine binary (hark-capture or harkd) in a minimal signed .app bundle with NSAudioCaptureUsageDescription so Core Audio Process Taps can acquire and retain the kTCCServiceAudioCapture grant.

nodes.name: .understandignore
nodes.summary: Gitignore-style exclude list for the Understand-Anything analyzer; scopes the scan to code by excluding build artifacts (.build/, .angular/) and all docs/markdown.

nodes.name: config.json
nodes.summary: Single-key config for the Understand-Anything analyzer, setting the output language to English.

nodes.name: Package.swift
nodes.summary: Swift Package Manager manifest for the Hark engine, declaring four executables (hark-bench, hark-engine, hark-capture, harkd) plus the HarkCore/HarkCapture libraries and pinning WhisperKit, swift-nio, FluidAudio, swift-transformers, and swift-crypto.
nodes.languageNotes: SPM manifest is itself Swift code; dependencies are pinned exactly or by SemVer range with inline rationale tied to ADRs and privacy rules.

nodes.name: .gitkeep
nodes.summary: Empty placeholder that keeps the engine/Results/ directory (where HarkBench writes RTF benchmark JSON) tracked in git.

nodes.name: main.swift
nodes.summary: Phase 0 Real-Time-Factor harness binary: loads WhisperKit, slides a 30s/5s-hop window over an input audio file, measures per-window transcription wall-clock, and emits a PASS/FAIL RTF report as JSON to stdout and engine/Results/.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses top-level code in main.swift (implicit @main); Codable structs with snake_case key-encoding strategy produce the report JSON.

nodes.name: detectChip
nodes.summary: Shells out to sysctl machdep.cpu.brand_string to read the Apple Silicon chip name for the benchmark hardware report.

nodes.name: percentile
nodes.summary: Computes a percentile of a Double array via linear interpolation between ranks; used for RTF p50/p95/p99 stats.

nodes.name: gitShortSha
nodes.summary: Runs git rev-parse --short HEAD against the repo to stamp the benchmark result filename, falling back to "nogit" on any failure.

nodes.name: CapturePipeline.swift
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the capture path: mic + system-audio backends → per-source Resampler → FIFO → 100ms pump → Mixer → optional WAV writer and Float-frame streaming sink for harkd.
nodes.languageNotes: FIFO drain uses an NSLock and a DispatchSourceTimer pump; FIFO append is keyed by ReferenceWritableKeyPath. Backend selected at runtime via the SystemAudioCapturing existential.

nodes.name: CapturePipeline
nodes.summary: Final class that wires mic/system capture to resampling, FIFO buffering, a 100ms pump, soft-clipping mix, and WAV/streaming sinks; emits a per-second JSON heartbeat with underrun and peak stats.

nodes.name: Options
nodes.summary: Configuration struct for CapturePipeline: which sources to capture, optional WAV output URL, optional Float-frame sink, and pump/underrun frame sizes.

nodes.name: CoreAudioProcessTap.swift
nodes.summary: Selectable (HARK_CAPTURE_BACKEND=tap) system-audio backend using macOS 14.4+ Core Audio Process Taps: builds a global tap + private aggregate device, runs a dedicated CFRunLoop for HAL notifications, and delivers PCM buffers from a realtime IOProc.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy C-style HAL interop (AudioObjectID property reads, CFRunLoop, dlopen TCC SPI via PermissionGate); IOProc block avoids touching self on the realtime thread.

nodes.name: CoreAudioProcessTap
nodes.summary: SystemAudioCapturing implementation over Core Audio Process Taps; manages tap/aggregate/IOProc lifecycle, a dedicated HAL run loop, and TCC audio-capture permission, with extensive HARK_TAP_DEBUG diagnostics.

nodes.name: MicCapture.swift
nodes.summary: Microphone capture via AVAudioEngine: installs a tap on the input node and forwards native-format PCM buffers to a caller closure on the Core Audio thread.

nodes.name: MicCapture
nodes.summary: Final class wrapping an AVAudioEngine input tap; exposes the native source format and start/stop that deliver AVAudioPCMBuffers to a BufferHandler.

nodes.name: Mixer.swift
nodes.summary: Sums two 16 kHz mono Float32 streams, applies tanh soft-clip, scales to Int16, and tracks frames-written / per-source underrun / peak-amplitude stats.

nodes.name: Mixer
nodes.summary: Final class that mixes one aligned chunk from each enabled source into Int16 PCM, counting underruns only for enabled-but-missing sources and updating Stats.

nodes.name: PermissionGate.swift
nodes.summary: TCC permission gate for capture: pure preflight checks plus active requests for Microphone and Screen Recording, and a dev-only private-SPI path (dlopen TCC) for the kTCCServiceAudioCapture permission behind HARK_ENABLE_TCC_SPI.
nodes.languageNotes: Bridges async permission callbacks with withCheckedContinuation; the private-API section resolves TCCAccessPreflight/TCCAccessRequest by symbol name via dlopen/dlsym.

nodes.name: PermissionGate
nodes.summary: Namespace enum exposing check(), ensureGranted(), requestMicrophone(), and the dev-only private-SPI audio-capture preflight/request used by the Core Audio tap path.

nodes.name: Status
nodes.summary: Value struct holding mic/screen grant flags with derived allGranted and an exit code; an extension prints a human-readable report with remediation steps.

nodes.name: Resampler.swift
nodes.summary: Wraps AVAudioConverter to convert arbitrary-input PCM to 16 kHz mono Float32, sizing the output buffer generously and reporting the actual converted frame count.

nodes.name: Resampler
nodes.summary: Final class wrapping AVAudioConverter; failable init builds the 16 kHz mono target, and convert() handles rate conversion and channel downmix per buffer.

nodes.name: SystemAudioCapturing.swift
nodes.summary: Protocol abstracting the two system-audio backends (ScreenCaptureKit SystemAudioTap and Core Audio CoreAudioProcessTap) so CapturePipeline can swap them via a one-line factory change.
nodes.languageNotes: An AnyObject-constrained protocol used as an existential (`any SystemAudioCapturing`) — Swift's equivalent of a Java interface-typed field selected at runtime.

nodes.name: SystemAudioCapturing
nodes.summary: Protocol declaring sourceFormat plus start(onBuffer:)/stop() — the seam both system-audio capture backends conform to.

nodes.name: SystemAudioTap.swift
nodes.summary: Default system-audio backend using ScreenCaptureKit (SCStream): captures audio under the Screen Recording TCC grant by running a deliberately tiny no-op video stream and copying audio CMSampleBuffers to AVAudioPCMBuffers.
nodes.languageNotes: Bridges SCK's async setup to a sync start() via DispatchSemaphore; conforms to NSObject + SCStreamOutput; copies samples with CMSampleBufferCopyPCMDataIntoAudioBufferList to outlive the callback.

nodes.name: SystemAudioTap
nodes.summary: SCStreamOutput-conforming SystemAudioCapturing backend that configures an audio+minimal-video SCStream, latches the delivered format on the first buffer, and forwards copied PCM buffers to the handler.

nodes.name: VAD.swift
nodes.summary: Voice Activity Detection: a VAD protocol plus an initial energy-based EnergyVAD with hangover (RMS over 100ms frames, silence/speech state machine) so a Silero CoreML implementation can drop in later without touching the sliding-window driver.
nodes.languageNotes: Protocol-behind-impl design (ADR-0008 §3): mutating classify(_:) lets the energy gate carry hangover state, keeping the rest of the pipeline indifferent to the VAD implementation.

nodes.name: EnergyVAD
nodes.summary: Energy-based VAD with hangover: computes per-frame RMS and runs a silence/speech state machine with a hangover count so word-internal stop consonants don't terminate an utterance.

nodes.name: VAD
nodes.summary: Protocol abstracting frame-batch voice activity classification so the pipeline can swap the energy gate for Silero CoreML later.

nodes.name: VaultWriter.swift
nodes.summary: Writes a finished meeting to the vault as markdown (ADR-0015 front-matter + blockquoted transcript) and git-commits it, plus appends summary/translation sections; runs only at capture.stop, never on the hot path, and never deletes or rewrites existing files.
nodes.languageNotes: A Sendable struct (not an actor) with no mutable state; shells out to local git via Foundation.Process (no remote, no push) and suffixes -2/-3 on filename collisions to honor the never-rewrite vault rule.

nodes.name: VaultWriter
nodes.summary: Stateless Sendable writer: renders meeting markdown, writes + git-commits the vault file, and appends summary/translation sections with pure static merge helpers.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes a new meeting markdown file to the vault (collision-suffixed) and git-commits it, returning the resulting path and stats.

nodes.name: renderMarkdown
nodes.summary: Renders the full meeting markdown document: ADR-0015 YAML front-matter plus the ## Transcript body of blockquoted, speaker-labeled utterances.

nodes.name: WebSocketServer.swift
nodes.summary: Localhost-only WebSocket server on Swift NIO: binds 127.0.0.1, rejects non-loopback connections, upgrades HTTP GET to WebSocket, runs the NIO handler chain, and dispatches one-JSON-message-per-text-frame to a weakly-held EngineSession via the WebSocketDelegate.
nodes.languageNotes: NIO ChannelHandler chain (HTTPServerProtocolUpgrader to WSFrameDecoder to AggregatingHandler to AppHandler); the AppHandler holds a weak EngineSession so the server can be wired before the engine is ready.

nodes.name: HarkdWebSocketServer
nodes.summary: The NIO server: binds the loopback channel on an ephemeral or specified port, installs the WebSocket upgrade handler chain, and exposes the bound port and a weak delegate.

nodes.name: HarkdWSAppHandler
nodes.summary: NIO ChannelInboundHandler at the tail of the chain: decodes incoming WebSocket text frames, runs the server-initiated heartbeat ping, and forwards connect/message/disconnect events to the delegate.

nodes.name: WebSocketClient
nodes.summary: Per-connection client handle wrapping the NIO channel, used by the engine to send frames to and broadcast across connected UI clients.

nodes.name: WebSocketDelegate
nodes.summary: Delegate protocol the server calls on connect, inbound text, and disconnect, implemented by the adapter that hops events onto the EngineSession actor.

nodes.name: WireProtocol.swift
nodes.summary: JSON envelope + payload Codables for the WebSocket API: the versioned WireEnvelope wrapper, every outbound event payload (meta.*, capture.*, segment.*, meeting.*, rag.*, warning, error), and every inbound command, against the contract source-of-truth.
nodes.languageNotes: Property names stay camelCase (Swift idiom); the snake_case wire form is produced by the encoder's keyEncodingStrategy at the call site. Indeterminate progress encodes fraction as JSON null, not a dropped key.

nodes.name: WireEnvelope
nodes.summary: Generic Encodable envelope carrying v, id, type (ns.action), ISO-8601-ms timestamp, and a typed payload that every outbound message wraps.

nodes.name: SegmentPayload
nodes.summary: Encodable payload for segment.partial/segment.final frames carrying utterance_id, timing, text, speaker, and translation fields.

nodes.name: MetaModelProgressPayload
nodes.summary: Encodable meta.model_progress payload whose fraction encodes as JSON null during the indeterminate ANE-compile phase so the UI shows a spinner, not a 0% bar.

nodes.name: CaptureStartCommand
nodes.summary: Decodable inbound capture.start command carrying source toggles (mic/system) and the translation request options.

nodes.name: SlidingWindow.swift
nodes.summary: Speech-gated 30s window with 5s hop plus utterance reconciliation: accumulates VAD-passed frames, fires per-hop transcription, and resolves whether consecutive-window segments are the same utterance via overlap/max-denominator identity (ADR-0009), minting or preserving utterance_ids.
nodes.languageNotes: Not thread-safe on its own — lives inside EngineSession's actor which serializes all mutations. The max-denominator identity rule (v2) closed the engulfment hole where a long re-segmented window hijacked a short entry's UUID.

nodes.name: UtteranceLedger
nodes.summary: The utterance identity ledger: resolves a segment to an existing or fresh utterance_id by overlap/max-denominator scoring, tracks finalization and supersession events, and prunes orphans aging out of the active window.

nodes.name: SlidingWindowBuffer
nodes.summary: Ring-style audio buffer that accumulates speech-gated frames into a 30s window and pops the latest window for transcription once a 5s hop is ready, mapping window offsets to absolute session time.

nodes.name: resolve
nodes.summary: Core identity resolver: scores a new segment's interval against existing ledger entries by overlap divided by the longer interval, returning the matched utterance_id or minting a fresh one.

nodes.name: extendFinalizedIfGrown
nodes.summary: Grows an already-finalized utterance in place when a later window produces a longer, overlapping version of the same text, returning its utterance_id for re-emission.

nodes.name: HarkCaptureTests.swift
nodes.summary: Placeholder smoke test that asserts the HarkCapture test target compiles before the per-component capture tests land.

nodes.name: WAVWriterTests.swift
nodes.summary: Round-trip tests for HarkCore.WAVWriter: writes Int16 samples, then asserts the 44-byte header and payload byte count are valid.

nodes.name: AudioPersistenceTests.swift
nodes.summary: Tests for opt-in meeting-audio persistence (AudioStore) and the keep_audio privacy gate (ADR-0027), driving the production store against a temp .audio/ dir and proving the gate-off path touches nothing.

nodes.name: CommitWatermarkTests.swift
nodes.summary: Regression coverage for ADR-0019's region-based finalize-once model, exercising the pure EngineSession.commitDecision and a faithful in-test reimplementation of the watermark advance without a live WhisperKit pipeline.

nodes.name: DedupTests.swift
nodes.summary: Regression coverage for the at-stop, interval-based, time-gated re-emission collapse (EngineSession.collapseReemissions), proving repeated copies collapse while identical text spoken far apart survives.

nodes.name: EmbedderTests.swift
nodes.summary: Coverage for the vault-RAG text embedder (ADR-0032): always-on pure pipeline math (masked mean-pooling, L2-normalization, prefix selection, MLMultiArray bridging) plus a gated on-device cross-lingual sanity test.

nodes.name: MeetingTranscriptTests.swift
nodes.summary: Coverage for the meeting.transcript mapping (EngineSession.transcriptUtterances), driving the production mapping over VaultWriter.Utterance inputs so the emit path and the test share one definition.

nodes.name: ModelProgressTests.swift
nodes.summary: Tests the first-run model-load progress path: the pure ModelProgressThrottle.decide rate-limit (never dropping a phase transition) and MetaModelProgressPayload encoding fraction as JSON null in the indeterminate state.

nodes.name: HarkEngine.swift
nodes.summary: Phase 1 batch transcription CLI (hark-engine): takes an audio file, runs WhisperKit, and emits structured JSON segments matching the WebSocket API contract's segment.final shape (speaker/translation as null).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses ArgumentParser's AsyncParsableCommand (@main) so argv is reflected into command struct properties, the Swift analogue of Spring's @Value-bound request beans.

nodes.name: HarkEngineCommand
nodes.summary: AsyncParsableCommand that parses CLI flags, loads WhisperKit, transcribes the input file, and writes the JSON EngineReport to stdout or --output.

nodes.name: EngineReport
nodes.summary: Codable top-level JSON output model bundling EngineMeta plus the array of EngineSegment results.

nodes.name: EngineSegment
nodes.summary: Codable per-segment record matching the WebSocket segment.final payload, with speaker and translation emitted as JSON null in Phase 1.

nodes.name: Diarizer.swift
nodes.summary: Thin actor wrapping FluidAudio's OfflineDiarizerManager, confining the loaded CoreML models to one isolation domain; runs a whole-meeting offline diarization pass only from EngineSession.flushOnStop.
nodes.languageNotes: Single-collaborator actor that serializes every call to a heavyweight non-Sendable manager, the idiomatic Swift alternative to manual locking.

nodes.name: Diarizer
nodes.summary: Actor owning an OfflineDiarizerManager; its diarize(_:sampleRate:) method runs FluidAudio's offline VBx pipeline over 16 kHz mono audio and returns exclusive speaker segments.

nodes.name: DiarizerLoader.swift
nodes.summary: Downloads (one-time from HuggingFace) and loads FluidAudio's offline diarization CoreML models into Hark's app-support models dir, then builds a ready OfflineDiarizerManager.
nodes.languageNotes: Forces the model cache under ~/Library/Application Support/Hark/Models per hard rule #2 by passing Hark's models root to OfflineDiarizerModels.load(from:).

nodes.name: LoadedDiarizer
nodes.summary: Result wrapper around a ready OfflineDiarizerManager with cold-start timing, produced by the loader's two-phase download-then-build flow.

nodes.name: EmbedderLoader.swift
nodes.summary: Downloads (one-time), ANE-compiles, and builds a CoreMLTextEmbedder for the vault-RAG default model, forcing both the CoreML package and tokenizer files to cache under Hark's app-support dir.
nodes.languageNotes: Constructs HubApi(downloadBase:) so every swift-transformers snapshot lands in Hark's dir; exactly one network event (first-run snapshot), offline thereafter.

nodes.name: LoadedEmbedder
nodes.summary: Result of loadTextEmbedder carrying the ready CoreMLTextEmbedder, its model descriptor, and load timing for cold-start logging.

nodes.name: EmbedderModels.swift
nodes.summary: Curated, local-only registry of text-embedding models for vault RAG (ADR-0032): immutable descriptors pinning repo, revision, tokenizer family, and 384-dim invariant. Data only, no behavior.
nodes.languageNotes: Enum-backed registry of immutable Sendable config records, the Swift analogue of a @ConfigurationProperties list of model descriptors.

nodes.name: EmbedderModel
nodes.summary: Immutable Sendable descriptor for one curated embedder: stable id, HuggingFace repo, pinned revision, dim, and tokenizer convention.

nodes.name: EngineSession.swift
nodes.summary: harkd's brain: the actor that wires Capture to VAD to SlidingWindow to WhisperKit to WebSocket emit, owns the full transcription session lifecycle, dispatches all inbound commands, and runs the post-stop diarization, dedup, vault-write, and speaker-enrollment passes.
nodes.languageNotes: Modeled as a Swift actor so all session-state mutations serialize on the actor's executor without explicit locks; the hot path hops capture-thread frames in via Task{ await session.ingest(...) }.

nodes.name: EngineSession
nodes.summary: The session actor: dispatches capture/bookmark/speaker/summary/translation/rag commands, drives the sliding-window transcription hot path, and runs flush-on-stop diarization, dedup, vault persistence, and speaker matching.

nodes.name: FinalizedUtterance
nodes.summary: Value type for a committed utterance carried through the at-stop dedup, collapse-reemissions, and speaker-labeling passes.

nodes.name: handleInbound
nodes.summary: Top-level inbound WebSocket message dispatcher that decodes the envelope type and routes to the per-command dispatch methods (capture, bookmark, speaker rename, summary, translation, rag).

nodes.name: runTranscription
nodes.summary: Per-hop transcription driver: runs WhisperKit over the latest window, normalizes segments to session time, reconciles against the UtteranceLedger, and emits partial/final WebSocket frames.

nodes.name: flushOnStop
nodes.summary: Capture-stop finalization: drains in-flight transcription, runs the offline diarization pass, dedups and collapses re-emissions, persists the meeting, and emits the meeting.saved/meeting.transcript frames.

nodes.name: commitDecision
nodes.summary: Pure static decision for the commit-watermark finalization model (ADR-0019): given a segment start and commit horizon, decide whether to finalize the region exactly once behind the monotonic committedUpTo watermark.

nodes.name: collapseReemissions
nodes.summary: Pure static at-stop pass that collapses time-gated re-emissions of the same spoken sentence (distinct utterance_ids from coarse re-segmentation) while preserving identical text spoken far apart.

nodes.name: transcriptUtterances
nodes.summary: Pure static mapping from deduped, speaker-labeled vault utterances to the meeting.transcript wire payload so the UI can replace the on-screen transcript to match the saved file.

nodes.name: runDiarizationPass
nodes.summary: Runs the offline Diarizer over the full session audio and assigns exclusive speaker segments to finalized utterances by overlap, producing Speaker N labels for the vault file and meeting roster.

nodes.name: HarkdCommand.swift
nodes.summary: Entry point for the harkd streaming daemon: binds the WebSocket server and writes the engine.port file immediately, loads WhisperKit behind the running server, wires the EngineSession, and handles SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown.
nodes.languageNotes: AsyncParsableCommand daemon; the WSDelegateAdapter bridges the NIO WebSocketDelegate callbacks onto the EngineSession actor, and ModelProgressThrottle rate-limits the per-byte/per-percent load callbacks.

nodes.name: HarkdCommand
nodes.summary: AsyncParsableCommand that boots the daemon: parses --port/--port-file/--verbose, starts the server, writes the port file, loads the model, and blocks on shutdown signals.

nodes.name: ModelProgressThrottle
nodes.summary: Rate-limit gate in front of the model-progress actor hop: drops the flood of per-byte/per-percent download callbacks while never dropping a phase transition.

nodes.name: WSDelegateAdapter
nodes.summary: Bridges the NIO WebSocketDelegate connect/disconnect/message callbacks onto the EngineSession actor via Task hops.

nodes.name: RagChunker.swift
nodes.summary: Stateless, pure utility that splits a vault markdown note into overlapping, heading-aware text windows sized under the embedder's 512-token cap, lifting YAML front-matter into metadata rather than embedding it.
nodes.languageNotes: Enum-namespaced stateless functions (no actor, no I/O), value-to-value so unit tests drive it deterministically with literal markdown; approximates tokens at ~4 chars/token for EN/VI/TH.

nodes.name: RagChunker
nodes.summary: Enum namespace of pure chunking functions turning one markdown file into heading-breadcrumbed, overlapping embeddable windows with stable content-addressed chunk ids.

nodes.name: RagChunk
nodes.summary: One embeddable unit of a note with a stable content-addressed chunkId (hash of notePath, charStart, and content), heading breadcrumb, and char offsets.

nodes.name: RagIndex.swift
nodes.summary: Brute-force in-memory cosine vector store for vault RAG, persisted as vectors.bin + meta.jsonl + manifest.json under app-support; an actor serializing the background indexer and foreground query path, storing offsets/pointers only and never raw note text.
nodes.languageNotes: Actor as the single owner of the mutable vector matrix; brute-force dot product over pre-normalized 384-dim vectors stays under 80 ms at <=50k chunks, deferring any ANN dependency.

nodes.name: RagIndex
nodes.summary: Actor vector store: loads/persists the flat index files and runs brute-force cosine search returning RagSearchHit/RagRetrievedChunk results.

nodes.name: RagChunkMeta
nodes.summary: Codable per-chunk metadata line (offsets and pointers only: chunkId, notePath, headingPath, char range, contentHash) parallel to a row in vectors.bin.

nodes.name: RagManifest
nodes.summary: Codable index manifest recording modelId, revision, dim, schemaVersion, chunkCount, and per-file content hashes for the incremental change-gate.

nodes.name: RagIndexer.swift
nodes.summary: Vault-RAG index coordinator: owns the indexing lifecycle off the live transcription path with a cold build on open, an FSEvents watcher with a 30s debounce + content-hash gate, a manual rebuild entry point, and graceful degradation when the embedder is absent.
nodes.languageNotes: Bridges the C FSEvents stream (on a dedicated DispatchQueue) into the RagIndex actor; a lock guards only the small dirty-set + timer state while all read/chunk/embed/store work runs async off the FSEvents queue.

nodes.name: RagIndexer
nodes.summary: Actor coordinator wiring the FSEvents watcher, debounce timer, chunker, and embedder around the RagIndex store; drains dirty paths and re-indexes changed .md files.

nodes.name: FSWatcher
nodes.summary: Wraps the C FSEventStream on a dedicated DispatchQueue, surfacing vault-root file changes to the indexer's debounced re-index callback.

nodes.name: SpeakerEnrollment.swift
nodes.summary: Local voiceprint store and matcher (ADR-0026): persists a per-person 256-dim centroid under vault/.speakers/ when the user names a speaker post-stop, then auto-recognizes that voice in future meetings via cosine distance — never networked, never logged.
nodes.languageNotes: A Sendable struct (not an actor) because it holds no in-memory state — every call reads the directory fresh and writes atomically; EngineSession (an actor) is the single serializing call site.

nodes.name: SpeakerStore
nodes.summary: Sendable struct over a directory of JSON voiceprint files: enrolls named speakers, lists enrolled speakers, and matches a query centroid to the nearest enrolled speaker by cosine distance.

nodes.name: EnrolledSpeaker
nodes.summary: Codable record of one enrolled person: display name plus the accumulated voiceprint samples used to build the matching centroid.

nodes.name: TextEmbedder.swift
nodes.summary: On-device CoreML text embedding for vault RAG (ADR-0032): a TextEmbedder protocol plus a CoreMLTextEmbedder actor mapping a string to an L2-normalized 384-dim vector via e5 prefix, offline tokenize, fixed tensors, ANE inference, and masked mean-pooling.
nodes.languageNotes: Actor as single owner of the stateful non-Sendable MLModel; the pure pad/pool/normalize math is split into static functions so EmbedderTests can drive the pipeline without the real .mlpackage.

nodes.name: CoreMLTextEmbedder
nodes.summary: Actor conforming to TextEmbedder: applies the e5 query/passage prefix, tokenizes offline, runs ANE inference, and masked-mean-pools to a unit-length 384-dim vector.

nodes.name: TextEmbedder

tour.title: App Launch: Electron Main
tour.description: Start where the OS starts the app. The Electron main process bootstraps Hark: it ensures the user's vault directory exists, spawns the harkd Swift sidecar, creates the main window plus the menu-bar tray, and wires the IPC handlers that bridge the renderer to preferences, the LLM layer, and RAG retrieval. This single file is the conductor of the whole desktop app, so it is the best vantage point to see how the UI shell, the engine sidecar, and the privacy-guarded egress paths all connect.

tour.title: Spawning the Engine Sidecar
tour.description: Hark's transcription brain runs in a separate process — a signed Swift binary called harkd — not inside Electron. From Step 1's bootstrap, harkd-spawn resolves the signed binary path, launches it as a child process, and supervises it; port-file then polls the file that harkd writes once it is listening. This is the handshake that lets a JavaScript app and a native Swift daemon find each other without hardcoding a port.
tour.languageLesson: Rather than agree on a fixed port (which could clash), the sidecar binds an OS-assigned port and writes it to a file as JSON; the parent polls that file with a timeout. This file-based rendezvous is a common pattern for decoupling a supervisor process from an ephemeral child server.

tour.title: The harkd Daemon Entry Point
tour.description: Now cross the process boundary into Swift. HarkdCommand is harkd's entry point: it binds the WebSocket server and writes the engine.port file from Step 2 immediately, loads WhisperKit behind the already-running server, wires up the EngineSession, and handles SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown. The WebSocketServer itself is loopback-only — it binds 127.0.0.1, rejects any non-loopback connection, and dispatches one JSON message per text frame to the session. Binding the port before the heavy model load is what lets the UI connect and show a loading state instead of timing out.
tour.languageLesson: Swift NIO is an event-driven, non-blocking network framework (think Netty for Swift). The server is built as a handler chain that upgrades an HTTP GET into a WebSocket and pushes frames through pipeline stages — the same channel-pipeline model Java developers know from Netty.

tour.title: Engine Build & Dependency Map
tour.description: Before tracing what harkd does at runtime, see how it is assembled. The SwiftPM manifest declares four executables (hark-bench, hark-engine, hark-capture, and the harkd daemon you just entered) plus the HarkCore and HarkCapture libraries, and pins the heavyweight on-device dependencies: WhisperKit for ASR, swift-nio for the WebSocket server, FluidAudio for diarization, swift-transformers, and swift-crypto. This manifest is the map of the engine's moving parts and explains why each Sources/ folder exists.
tour.languageLesson: Package.swift is both build config and executable Swift — the manifest is real code evaluated by SwiftPM. A multi-target package lets one repo ship several CLIs (the capture/bench tools) alongside the production daemon while sharing core libraries, similar to a Maven multi-module project.

tour.title: Capturing & Mixing Audio
tour.description: A meeting begins with sound. The CapturePipeline orchestrates two backends — the microphone (via AVAudioEngine) and system audio (via ScreenCaptureKit) — resampling each source to 16 kHz mono and pumping 100ms chunks into the Mixer, which sums the two streams, soft-clips, and converts to the format WhisperKit expects. PermissionGate guards all of this behind macOS TCC grants for Microphone and Screen Recording. This is the raw-audio front door of the entire system, and it is the only place audio is ever touched before transcription.
tour.languageLesson: Capturing system audio on macOS has no clean public API, so SystemAudioTap runs a deliberately tiny no-op ScreenCaptureKit video stream just to obtain audio frames under the Screen Recording permission — a well-known workaround for an OS limitation rather than a hack specific to this codebase.

tour.title: Loading the WhisperKit Model
tour.description: On-device ASR needs a model in memory before it can transcribe. ModelLoader is a shared two-phase loader: Phase A downloads the WhisperKit model files with a progress bar, and Phase B prewarms and compiles them onto the Apple Neural Engine while emitting heartbeat and progress pulses (which drive the UI's loading overlay from Step 9). HarkPaths is the single authority for where those models live — under ~/Library/Application Support/Hark, never in the vault — enforcing the hard rule that rebuildable caches stay out of the user's notes.

tour.title: Transcription: VAD, Window, Finalize
tour.description: EngineSession is harkd's brain — an actor that wires Capture to VAD to the SlidingWindow to WhisperKit to the WebSocket emit, owning the whole session lifecycle. VAD gates out silence using an energy-based detector with hangover, so only speech reaches the model. SlidingWindow runs a speech-gated 30-second window with a 5-second hop, firing per-hop transcriptions and reconciling whether consecutive windows describe the same utterance — minting or preserving stable utterance IDs so live captions don't flicker or duplicate. This is the heart of how raw audio becomes finalized text.
tour.languageLesson: EngineSession is a Swift `actor`, which serializes all access to its mutable state so the capture thread, the WebSocket thread, and the transcription task can't race. Coming from Java, think of it as an object whose every method is implicitly synchronized — but enforced by the compiler via async access rather than locks.

tour.title: The Wire Protocol Contract
tour.description: harkd and the UI talk over WebSocket using a strict JSON contract, and this contract has two synchronized halves. On the Swift side, WireProtocol defines the versioned envelope and every payload — meta.*, capture.*, segment.*, meeting.*, rag.*, warning, error — plus every inbound command. On the TypeScript side, engine.types mirrors those exact frames, segments, and speaker shapes for the renderer. Understanding this pair is what makes the rest of the data flow legible: every transcript line the user sees started as one of these frames.
tour.languageLesson: Both sides hand-maintain matching types against one source-of-truth contract, with the wire shape in snake_case. There is no generated stub layer (unlike gRPC/protobuf), so the discipline is: a frame only exists when the Swift Codable, the TS interface, and both handlers all agree.

tour.title: Live Captions in the Renderer
tour.description: Back in the Angular UI, EngineService owns the WebSocket connection to harkd: it dispatches each incoming wire frame into Angular signals (capture state, heartbeat, segments, bookmarks, meeting-saved) and sends commands back. AppComponent is the root shell that consumes those signals to render the live transcript and drive every panel, while transcript-line presents a single line with its timestamp, speaker color, optional translation, and partial caret. This is where the segment frames from Step 8 finally become the captions a user reads in real time.
tour.languageLesson: Angular 21 signals give EngineService a reactive push model: incoming frames update signals, and OnPush components re-render automatically off those reads — no manual change detection. It is the same observable-state idea as RxJS subjects, but with finer-grained, synchronous dependency tracking.

tour.title: On Stop: Diarize, Save, Enroll
tour.description: When the user stops capture, EngineSession runs its post-stop passes — none of which touch the live hot path. Diarizer wraps FluidAudio's offline diarization in a single actor to label who spoke when. VaultWriter then writes the finished meeting as markdown (front-matter plus a blockquoted transcript) and git-commits it, never deleting or rewriting existing files. SpeakerEnrollment optionally persists a local 256-dim voiceprint under vault/.speakers/ so a named speaker is auto-recognized in future meetings — entirely local, never networked. This is how a live session becomes a permanent, speaker-labeled note in the user's vault.

tour.title: The Only Network Egress
tour.description: Everything so far has stayed on the machine. The single exception is the explicit, user-invoked LLM path, and it lives entirely in the Electron main process — never the renderer. The LLM orchestrator handles summarize, translation, and Q&A, enforcing redact-before-cloud and metadata-only logging; the redactor collapses emails, phones, money, URLs, and roster names into category placeholders before any text leaves; and the RAG loopback guard asserts that any vault-retrieval endpoint resolves to a loopback host so retrieval traffic never escapes. This trio is where privacy is enforced in code, not just policy.

tour.title: Packaging the App
tour.description: Finally, see how all these pieces ship as one product. The electron-builder config produces a signed, notarization-ready macOS .app/dmg/zip for arm64 — bundling the compiled Angular renderer, the Electron main process, and the statically-linked harkd sidecar from Steps 2-10 together. It applies the hardened runtime, inherit-entitlement signing for the sidecar, and TCC usage strings for the mic/screen permissions from Step 5, with no auto-update, no publish, and no telemetry. This closes the loop on how Hark's local-first promises survive all the way into the distributed binary.
tour.languageLesson: macOS distribution requires the app to be code-signed and notarized by Apple, and an embedded helper binary (harkd) must be signed with inherited entitlements so it runs under the parent's hardened runtime. Disabling auto-update and publish here is a deliberate privacy choice: the app never phones home.
